item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Tshisekedi actually empowered an institution to constrain him when it did so, for example by protecting adverse court rulings, shielding parliamentary oversight, devolving real autonomy to local governments, or insulating audit bodies from presidential control. The positive record is mostly executive-hosted reform meetings and anti-corruption rhetoric, not durable institutional strengthening.","evidence":[{"title":"Le Chef de l’État a assisté à l’ouverture de la session extraordinaire du conseil supérieur de la Cour des comptes","publisher":"Présidence RDC","date":"2024-10-07","url":"https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes","summary":"Tshisekedi publicly backed the Court of Accounts’ control function, and the court said his support helped revive anti-corruption oversight and public-finance control. This is the clearest pro-evidence for oversight bodies, but it is still presidentially framed and does not show independence from the executive.","question_ids":["4B.4"]},{"title":"États généraux de la justice, Le Chef de l’État déclare : « notre justice sera purgée de ses fléaux »","publisher":"Présidence RDC","date":"2024-11-06","url":"https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/etats_generaux_de_la_justice_le_chef_de_l_etat_declare_notre_justice_sera_purgee_de_ses_fleaux","summary":"Tshisekedi opened a large justice-reform forum with about 3,500 judges, experts, activists, and academics, presenting it as a diagnosis of the justice system’s failures and a route to “renaissance.” This shows reform signaling, but not a demonstrated transfer of autonomy to the courts.","question_ids":["4B.4"]},{"title":"Kalemie - Conférence des gouverneurs","publisher":"Présidence RDC","date":"2024-11-27","url":"https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/kalemie_conference_des_gouverneurs_le_collectif_des_gouverneurs_de_province_soutien_lidee_dune_revision_ou_dun_changement_de_la_constitution","summary":"Tshisekedi urged provincial governors to use transparent and efficient practices, endorsed autonomous local revenue management, periodic evaluations, and possible IGTER audits. This is the best local-government/oversight signal I found, but it is still centrally driven and does not show independent local power insulated from the presidency.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.2"]},{"title":"Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/democratic-republic-congo/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says the judiciary, especially the Constitutional Court, is often seen as corrupt and politically manipulated, with bias against opposition and civil society; it also says military courts face interference from high-ranking military personnel. This is strong evidence against independent courts and oversight.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.3"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Human rights priorities for the government of Democratic Republic of Congo during President Tshisekedi’s second term","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-06-24","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr62/8155/2024/en/","summary":"Amnesty said Tshisekedi’s first-term pledges had produced little to no progress, and that the state needed to end the state of siege, fix prisons, stop arbitrary detention, and strengthen rule-of-law protections. This is negative evidence that the administration had not meaningfully strengthened independent institutions by mid-2024.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.3"]},{"title":"DRC: President Félix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-09-30","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/","summary":"Amnesty said the state of siege concentrated power in military and police officials, militarized everyday life, and coincided with a crackdown on dissent; it also said military courts handed down more than 100 death sentences after executions were reinstated. That points to coercive executive control, not stronger checks and balances.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.3"]},{"title":"A Human Rights Agenda for the Democratic Republic of Congo","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-06","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/human-rights-agenda-democratic-republic-congo","summary":"HRW said the administration had made little progress on promised systemic reforms and called for an independent, fair judiciary, anti-corruption safeguards, and stronger democratic institutions. This is not just a recommendation; it reflects HRW’s assessment that those institutions were not being strengthened in practice.","question_ids":["4B.4"]},{"title":"Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts- report","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-01-15","url":"https://theprint.in/world/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report/1925035/","summary":"A civil-society report said CENI failed to account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement, with calls for investigations into how election funds were managed. This is direct negative evidence for an oversight body that should have been transparent and accountable.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.1"]},{"title":"DR Congo constitutional court rejects petitions against provisional election results","publisher":"Reuters","date":"2024-01-10","url":"https://theprint.in/world/dr-congo-constitutional-court-rejects-petitions-against-provisional-election-results/1917177/","summary":"The Constitutional Court upheld Tshisekedi’s victory, but Reuters noted that main opposition figures refused to use the court because they did not trust state institutions. That is weakly negative for judicial independence and much more evidence of a court lacking credibility as a constraint.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.1"]}]}
